title: Vasuki and Mount Mandara at real scale
caption:
According to the Mahabharata, Vasuki was the rope used to churn the ocean of milk, wrapped around a mountain taller than ten Earths 🐍

🏔️ The Mahabharata gives Mount Mandara a height of 11,000 yojanas. At about 13 km per yojana, that's roughly 1,43,000 km, more than 11 Earths stacked up.
🌍 Even if Mandara were only as wide as Earth, one coil of Vasuki would be 40,000 km long, the length of the equator.
🐢 When the mountain began to sink, Vishnu took the form of Kurma and held it on his back.
💙 The poison that rose from the churning was drunk by Lord Shiva, turning his throat blue.
📍 Mandar Hill in Banka, Bihar, has spiral grooves that local tradition attributes to Vasuki.

Follow for more of India's epics, measured at real scale.
